disease_label_per_paper: Severe polymyositis in a metastatic colorectal cancer patient after chemotherapy
presentation_summary: 72-year-old woman with metastatic colorectal cancer and controlled nonerosive rheumatoid arthritis developed acute dysphagia and rapidly progressive proximal weakness seven days after the second oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy/bevacizumab administration.

Within one week she became unable to stand, walk, raise upper or lower limbs, or swallow saliva. She had mild diffuse myalgia, no fever, no respiratory difficulty, no joint pain, and normal cutaneous exam.

Initial evaluation showed MRC grade 4 bilateral proximal weakness, CRP 40 mg/dL, CK 8892 IU/L rising to 10000 IU/L despite hydration, normal renal/liver/thyroid function, and no clear infectious, neurologic, or cardiac explanation.
Muscle MRI, autoantibody panel, EMG limitations, final polymyositis diagnosis, high-dose methylprednisolone/IVIg treatment, and fatal outcome are confirmatory or non-ranking context.
